clips.text_zh: Doge 3日內上太空，你仲唔買？最衰都會郁上去啦，偷注少少再放就得，唔好變 SNL 2.0 🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Doge goes to fucking space in 3 days and you are not buying. If this shit explodes it will still move up, so why not ape a bit, then sell so it does not become SNL 2.0? Or maybe it will just start the hype again. Either way, the risk is small and the upside is real.
clips.source_hint: Biz OP hyping a Dogecoin catalyst tied to a space launch.

signal.rationale: OP is urging a small long into a known 3-day catalyst, then sell into hype.

clips.text_en_b2: Dogecoin is genuinely heading to space within the next three days, and yet people are still hesitant to get in. Even if the launch turns out to be a damp squib, the token will almost certainly bounce on the hype alone, so throwing a modest position at it makes sense. Take a small bet, bank the profits quickly, and avoid letting it become another Saturday Night Live disaster. At worst, the announcement reignites retail interest and sparks another leg up.
clips.text_en_c1: Dogecoin is, allegedly, heading to space within the next three days, and you are still sitting on the fence. Even in a worst-case scenario where the mission fails spectacularly, the resulting volatility is likely to drive the price upward for a brief window. The rational move, therefore, would be to allocate a modest position, ride the momentum, and exit before sentiment collapses — lest we witness a repeat of the infamous SNL disaster. Of course, should the launch generate renewed enthusiasm, one might simply hold. Either way, the downside risk appears negligible compared with the upside, which is hardly negligible at all.
clips.text_en_c2: Dogecoin is, by all credible indicators, poised to breach the thermosphere within seventy-two hours, and yet here you sit, conspicuously abstaining. Even in the bleakest scenario, where the venture collapses under its own absurdity, residual momentum will almost certainly propel the price upward, if only briefly. The prudent play, therefore, is a modest speculative position with a clearly defined exit, lest history rhyme with the SNL fiasco and retail capital evaporates once more. Should the launch prove anticlimactic, the prevailing optimism will likely reassert itself. Conversely, genuine traction would reignite the broader euphoria. Asymmetric risk, tangible upside.

clips.text_zh: 沙特東西輸油管被炸，沙特10%全球產能受影響，維修要6至12個月。今日油價反倒下插，wtf 🧐 等低位再long？
clips.text_en_b1: Big happening: 150 dollar oil soon? The Saudi east-west pipeline got hit. Saudi Arabia can no longer go around the Strait of Hormuz. Satellite pictures show the pipeline is damaged in many places, and a pump station may be hit too. AI estimates 6 to 12 months for repair. Saudi Arabia has 10 percent of global oil production. Ironically, oil dumped today.
clips.source_hint: Biz OP claiming a Saudi pipeline strike with multi-month repair time.

signal.rationale: Supply shock setup favours oil but OP notes price dumped anyway; also a classic gold hedge catalyst for the learner.

clips.text_en_b2: Brent crude touching 150 dollars a barrel now looks like a real possibility after the Saudi East-West pipeline suffered significant damage. Satellite imagery reveals multiple breach points along the route, while reports suggest a pump station was also struck, effectively closing off the bypass around the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts estimate repairs could take anywhere between six and twelve months, and Saudi Arabia controls roughly ten percent of global supply.
clips.text_en_c1: Are we witnessing the prelude to one-hundred-and-fifty-dollar oil? Saudi Arabia's east-west pipeline has suffered a substantial blow, effectively severing the kingdom's ability to circumvent the Strait of Hormuz. Satellite imagery reveals extensive damage across multiple sections of the infrastructure, with at least one pumping station reportedly compromised. Industry analysts estimate that full restoration could take anywhere between six and twelve months, a timeframe that would constrain roughly ten percent of global supply. Curiously, despite the magnitude of the disruption, prices have dipped intraday — a development that would warrant either aggressive buying at the dip or a serious reassessment of market positioning.
clips.text_en_c2: A consequential development, one that ought to have sent crude soaring: the Saudi East–West pipeline has reportedly sustained substantial damage, effectively neutering Riyadh's strategic workaround for the Strait of Hormuz. Satellite imagery corroborates multiple breach points along the artery, with at least one pump station plausibly compromised. Independent assessments, leveraging advanced modelling, project a remediation timeline of six to twelve months, a duration during which roughly ten percent of global supply remains imperilled. Yet, in a tableau of exquisite market irony, oil has dumped precipitously today. The contrarian instinct whispers to accumulate on weakness, to long into what may be a transient dislocation before fundamentals reassert their inexorable gravity.

clips.text_zh: 10年你淨係hold一樣，你揀BTC定黃金？好老土但我真係諗緊，萬一真係返美之前要跑贏通脵 😅
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? This came up on /biz/ today and every reply is the usual cope and maxis fighting. The split is roughly 60/40 for BTC in recent threads.
clips.source_hint: Biz OP asking which asset to hold for the next decade.
clips.text_en_b2: If you could only hold a single asset for the next decade, would your money go into Bitcoin or gold? The thread kicked off that exact debate on /biz/, and predictably it descended into the usual clash between gold bugs and Bitcoin maxis shouting cope at each other. Recent polls put the split at around sixty-forty in favour of BTC, though the gold camp argues the metal has weathered centuries of monetary experimentation.
clips.text_en_c1: A question that sounds almost trite yet warrants genuine consideration: were you compelled to hold a single asset for the next decade, would you select Bitcoin or gold? The thread on /biz/ has predictably devolved into the usual spectacle of maximalists and goldbugs trading ideological barbs, with little substantive analysis to be found. Recent polls suggest a roughly sixty-forty split in favour of BTC, though such figures reflect tribal allegiance more than rigorous reasoning. The real question, of course, is which instrument offers superior protection should monetary conditions deteriorate markedly before any hypothetical return to pre-inflation norms.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial question, freshly resurgent on the boards: should one, given a ten-year horizon and the constraint of a singular position, elect Bitcoin or gold? The thread has predictably devolved into the customary theatre, with maximalist partisans trading rhetorical volleys while the silent majority watches. Recent polling suggests a rough consensus, perhaps sixty-forty in favour of BTC, though such figures mean little against the vagaries of the next decade. What animates the inquiry, ostensibly, is the creeping anxiety over dollar debasement. Yet beneath the contrarian posturing lies a more elemental anxiety, namely, whether either asset class will meaningfully outpace the erosive tide of inflation.

clips.text_zh: 終於有人認AI model到樽頸，搞個self restraint嘅story出嚟呃VC錢。又係咁上下 🙏 我份工仲有幾耐？
clips.text_en_b1: So they are admitting AI models have plateaued and are making up some fake story about self restraint so they do not lose VC money. The cope is incredible. New model launches are basically the same benchmark numbers with a marketing spin. I am so tired of this talmudic bullshit.
clips.source_hint: /g/ OP calling out labs for plateaued AI progress.
clips.text_en_b2: It is genuinely refreshing to see labs openly admitting that frontier AI models have hit a plateau, though unsurprisingly they are spinning some elaborate tale about deliberate self-restraint to keep VC cheques rolling in. The cope has reached absurd levels, with each new release basically recycling identical benchmark scores wrapped in slick marketing language. Anyone paying attention can see the diminishing returns are real, yet the funding circus grinds on regardless.
clips.text_en_c1: At long last, insiders are openly conceding that frontier AI models have hit a discernible plateau, yet the corporate apparatus has spun an elaborate narrative about self-imposed restraint to preserve the illusion of inevitable progress. The cope, frankly, is breathtaking in its audacity: every successive launch repackages identical benchmark scores with a fresh veneer of marketing polish. Meanwhile, those of us whose livelihoods depend on these trajectories are left to contemplate how much runway remains before the venture capital well runs dry and the sector's frothy valuations undergo a long-overdue correction.
clips.text_en_c2: At long last, the prevailing orthodoxy concedes the inevitable: the frontier models have demonstrably plateaued, their incremental gains yielding diminishing returns against the colossal expenditure required to eke out marginal benchmark improvements. Rather than own this admission forthrightly, the incumbents have opted for the more palatable narrative of deliberate self-restraint, a sanitising conceit designed to mollify venture capital while preserving the illusion of imminent superintelligence. The contortions required to sustain this fiction border on the theological, hence the sardonic invocation of the talmudic. Meanwhile, the benchmarks themselves have calcified into marketing collateral, indistinguishable save for the typography. One wonders, with mounting unease, how long this elaborate charade can persist.

clips.text_zh: 21歲炒dogecoin贏錢，買咗condo，之後打回原形。依家返學做返100K USD份工，揹住學貸同卡數。又係另一個香港故事 🇭🇰
clips.text_en_b1: Stuck with a Condo. In 2021 when I was 22 I made a bunch of random crypto money from Dogecoin. I lived for two years with no job, perma vacation, dropped out of school and bought a condo for 230K USD. Eventually the money ran out. I went back to school, graduated, and now I make 100K a year in my condo.
clips.source_hint: Biz OP reflecting on crypto windfall turned into debt trap.

signal.rationale: Life story post, no setup — but mirrors the learner's own crypto path.

clips.text_en_b2: Back in 2021, when I was just 22, I struck it moderately lucky on Dogecoin and walked away with a ridiculous amount of money for someone my age. I promptly quit my job, dropped out of uni, and splashed out 230K USD on a condo, basically living a permanent holiday for two solid years. Predictably, the funds dried up eventually, and I had to crawl back to school, graduate, and accept a 100K-a-year salary just to keep the roof over my head.
clips.text_en_c1: The archetypal cautionary tale: at twenty-two, a speculative windfall from Dogecoin furnished two glorious years of perpetual vacation, an abandoned education, and a two-hundred-thirty-thousand-dollar condominium purchased on what proved to be borrowed euphoria. The inevitable reckoning arrived, funds depleted, and at twenty-seven I find myself indentured to a six-figure salary that services both student loans and accumulated credit card debt while I languish in the very asset I once celebrated. Hong Kong's housing trap claims yet another casualty — a cautionary reminder that timing the market and timing one's life seldom align.
clips.text_en_c2: Another cautionary tableau from the meme-asset generation: at twenty-two, serendipitous Dogecoin speculation furnished sufficient lucre to render conventional ambition obsolete. For two languorous years, the protagonist existed in a state of perma-vacation, forsaking academia, whereupon a condominium was acquired for a sum approximating 230K USD. The terminal phase proved inevitable: liquidity depleted, the gilded interlude concluded, and recourse was had to reinstatement at the educational institution from which departure had been so cavalierly effected. Graduation followed, as did employment yielding a six-figure salary, ostensibly the realisation of every millennial aspiration. Yet the conditional reality is rather more Sisyphean: a condominium encumbered by student obligations and revolving credit liabilities, with the protagonist, now twenty-seven, trapped within an inexorable cycle of labour, consumption, and repetition.

clips.text_zh: 83kg肥落65kg skinnyfat，再lean bulk到80kg。臥推1 plate，深蹲90kg，硬拉120kg。係咪可以開始cut？肥仔信今日又叫我加重量 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: How do I know when I have bulked enough to cut and escape skinnyfat? In May 2025 I was 83kg fat with almost no muscle. I cut aggressively until April 2026 and got down to 65kg skinnyfat, struggling to bench even the 20kg bar. Then I lean bulked to today.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ OP asking when to switch from lean bulk to cut.

signal.rationale: Body recomp question, no trade setup.

clips.text_en_b2: How on earth do you actually figure out when it is time to start cutting instead of continuing to bulk? Back in May 2025 I was carrying 83kg of pure blubber with virtually no muscle underneath. I committed to an aggressive cut that lasted until April 2026, dropping down to a miserable 65kg of classic skinnyfat territory where I could barely bench the empty 20kg bar.
clips.text_en_c1: At what precise inflection point does a former skinnyfat physique acquire sufficient muscle mass to warrant a cutting phase? In May 2025, I tipped the scales at a bloated eighty-three kilograms with negligible lean tissue. An aggressive caloric deficit spanning nearly a year reduced me to a gaunt sixty-five, at which point even a twenty-kilogram barbell felt insurmountable on the flat bench. Following a methodical lean bulk, I now stand at eighty kilograms, pressing one plate for three sets of eight, squatting ninety kilograms for similar volume, and pulling one-hundred-twenty on the deadlift — numbers which suggest readiness to cut.
clips.text_en_c2: The diagnostic conundrum for the formerly adipose, now merely lean-deficient: at what juncture does one transition from caloric surplus to aggressive catabolism without forfeiting the hard-won musculature? In May 2025, I presented as classically obese at 83 kilograms, adipose tissue constituting the predominant fraction of body mass. An aggressive, sustained cut culminated in April 2026, with my weight bottoming at 65 kilograms, though the regression was stark, my bench press reduced to the unadorned twenty-kilogram bar. Subsequently, a disciplined lean bulk restored me to 80 kilograms. Current metrics: a flat bench of one plate for triples of eight, a squat of ninety kilograms for triples of six, and a deadlift of 120 kilograms for triples of eight.
